svg.title: Lume Memory Saga & 4-Tier Atomic Memory Compactor — Evolution Benchmark Dashboard
svg.desc: Animated benchmark comparison across Baseline (Pre-R5), Round 5 (Segregated Mark-Sweep GC + Ownership v2), and Round 6 (4-Tier Atomic Memory Compactor) showing up to 31.8x latency speedup, 23.6x RAM reduction, and 200M to 1 allocation collapse.

g.text: Lume Memory Saga & 4-Tier Atomic Memory Compactor
Empirical Evolution on Intel Core Ultra 5 135U (WSL2 x86-64) · Baseline → Round 5 (Segregated Mark-Sweep GC) → Round 6 (Atomic Compactor Levels 0–3)
1. 4-Tier Atomic Memory Compactor — Register & Cell Bit Layout
1-cycle register pack/unpack (`sarq` / `leaq`) · 0 B heap for hot values · Beats Rust `String` (24 B + heap) on ≤7 B strings
LEVEL 1A · 63-BIT SIGNED INTEGER IN REGISTER (0 B HEAP · 1-CYCLE ARITHMETIC)
LEVEL 1B · INLINE SHORT STRING SSO ≤ 7 BYTES (0 B HEAP · 74.9%–94.9% OF STRINGS)
bytes [7..1]: Up to 7 Raw UTF-8 Bytes Inline
STAGE 0 & LEVEL 2 · STATIC .RODATA LITERALS, SINGLETON NIL & COMPACT CELLS
LEVEL 3 · COLD ARENA & .LCAPS/.LUMB LZ1 COMPACTOR (PROT_NONE LAZY PAGE THAW)
[LZ1\x1a · orig_len · fnv64] · 355 MB/s Pack · 975 MB/s Unpack · [C0009] @secret Guard
Paired medians of 7 alternating runs · Lower latency & drastically fewer heap allocations
3. Complete Memory (Peak RSS) & Allocation Evolution Across Generations
